problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $4\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(5,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ seconds.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration of a Particle Moving With Circular Motion
examples.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $\mathbf {r}(t)= 4(\cos 3t\,  \mathbf i + \sin 3t\, \mathbf j)$ meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
examples.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(4(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,i+12\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =(v(t))^{′} \\  & =(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,i+12\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-36\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i-36\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||a(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-36\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)^{2}+(-36\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{36}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡3t+{36}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡3t} \\  & =\sqrt{{36}^{2}} \\  & =36\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is $36\, \textrm{m/s}^2.$

Note that $||\mathbf a||$ is constant, but $\mathbf a$ is not.

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
\mathbf a = -\omega^2\mathbf r \qquad \Rightarrow \qquad ||\mathbf a|| = \omega^2||\mathbf r||.
$$

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=4\,\textrm m$ and the angular frequency $\omega = 3\,\textrm{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||\mathbf a|| = 3^2\cdot |4| = 36\, \textrm{m/s}^2.
$$

feedback.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi t\,j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-6\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi t\,i+6\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed, we calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||v(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-6\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi t)^{2}+(6\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36{\pi }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡2\pi t+36{\pi }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡2\pi t} \\  & =\sqrt{36{\pi }^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡2\pi t+{cos}^{2}⁡2\pi t)} \\  & =6\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the object is $6\pi \text{ m/s}.$

Note that the speed is constant, but the velocity is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
||v||=R|\omega |,
$$

where $R$ is the radius of the circle, and $\omega $ is the angular velocity.

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=3\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =2\pi \,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||v||=3\cdot |2\pi |=6\pi \text{ m/s}.
$$
